Name: Simple Desktop
Author: Xsyy
Description:
[center][size=6][b][color=#F2C879]Simple Desktop[/color][/b][/size]
[size=4][color=#8FDAC0]A little computer corner for your farmhouse. A very expensive hobby for your farmer.[/color][/size][/center]

[center][size=5][color=#D9B7FF]💜 If you enjoy my mods, please consider endorsing this mod. Thank you for your support! ⭐[/color][/size][/center]

Craft a computer, place it in your home, and open a desktop filled with farm information, collection records and playable games. Work your way through seven computer tiers to add recipe guides, a quest journal, music, shipping analytics and a larger game library.

Every computer has its own single-monitor design, a compact oak desk and a two-by-two tile footprint. Each tier shows only the apps and games it can actually use.

[heading][color=#8FDAC0]🛒 Where to buy your first computer[/color][/heading]
Visit [b]Robin's Carpenter's Shop in the Mountains[/b] and open her [b]regular shop menu[/b]. Buy the [b]Computer I Assembly Kit for 1,000,000g[/b], with one free backpack slot. The kit unlocks the recipe: craft your Computer I in the normal crafting menu using [b]one kit, 100 Hardwood, 20 Copper Bars, 30 Iron Bars, 10 Refined Quartz and 5 Battery Packs[/b]. Robin sells the kit; you craft the finished computer.

[heading][color=#F2C879]🖥️ Seven computers to build[/color][/heading]
Prices below are [b]cumulative gold milestones for one computer[/b]. Each tier keeps the capabilities of the tiers before it. Crafting materials are additional.

[list]
[*][b]Computer I — 1,000,000g total[/b]
Farm information, collection records, Chess and Reversi.[/*]
[*][b]Computer II — 2,500,000g total[/b]
Adds crafting and cooking guides, a read-only quest journal, Solitaire, Minesweeper and Memory Match. The upgrade kit costs 1,500,000g plus your Computer I.[/*]
[*][b]Computer III — 5,000,000g total[/b]
Adds unlocked music, access to the normal map, one-suit Spider Solitaire and Snake. The upgrade kit costs 2,500,000g plus your Computer II.[/*]
[*][b]Computer IV — 10,000,000g total[/b]
Adds shipping analytics, optional World Market access and 2048. The upgrade kit costs 5,000,000g plus your Computer III.[/*]
[*][b]Computer V — 25,000,000g total[/b]
Adds Motor Dash, Connect Four and Breakout. The upgrade kit costs 15,000,000g plus your Computer IV.[/*]
[*][b]Computer VI — 50,000,000g total[/b]
Adds Unblock, Checkpoint Race and native arcade practice. The upgrade kit costs 25,000,000g plus your Computer V.[/*]
[*][b]Computer VII — 100,000,000g total[/b]
Adds Cross Roads, Jigsaw Puzzle and Find the Treasure. The upgrade kit costs 50,000,000g plus your Computer VI.[/*]
[/list][heading][color=#8FDAC0]🛠️ Start at Robin's workshop[/color][/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Open Robin's normal shop and buy a [b]Computer I Assembly Kit[/b] for 1,000,000g. Leave one free backpack slot for the kit.[/*]
[*]Use the unlocked recipe in your normal crafting menu. The Computer I needs [b]one kit, 100 Hardwood, 20 Copper Bars, 30 Iron Bars, 10 Refined Quartz and 5 Battery Packs[/b].[/*]
[*]Place the computer as furniture and interact with it nearby to open its desktop.[/*]
[*]When you want the next tier, pick up your empty computer and carry it in your backpack to Robin. Select the next kit, review the computer being traded in, and confirm the exchange.[/*]
[*]Craft the next computer using its kit and materials. Repeat the chain to reach your chosen tier.[/*]
[/list]Every upgrade consumes the selected previous-tier computer and its listed gold difference. Each kit is single-use, so a known recipe alone does not bypass the progression. Every additional computer follows its own paid chain. Cancelling the exchange leaves your gold and computer untouched.

[heading][color=#9ACAF7]📖 Your farm, on your desktop[/color][/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Information:[/b] check your farmer's current farm details, date, weather, gold, energy and health.[/*]
[*][b]Farm Overview:[/b] after learning the vanilla Farm Computer recipe, check crops, watering, forage and ready machines separately for each farming location. Available on Computer I–VII.[/*]
[*][b]Collections:[/b] browse recorded shipments, fish catches, minerals and artifacts, with search and item icons. Mineral and artifact entries reflect discovery records rather than museum donations.[/*]
[*][b]Recipe guides:[/b] browse crafting and cooking recipes your farmer already knows. Check ingredients, backpack quantities and current craft availability. The guides are for reference; crafting stays in the normal game menu.[/*]
[*][b]Quest journal:[/b] read visible quests and special orders, their objectives, deadlines and rewards. Use the normal journal to claim rewards, cancel quests or manage them.[/*]
[*][b]Music:[/b] choose from songs you have unlocked through the game's jukebox list.[/*]
[*][b]Map:[/b] open the normal world map from your computer.[/*]
[*][b]Shipping analytics:[/b] review gold and item totals for up to 112 recorded shipping days. Records begin after installation; earlier shipping history is not reconstructed.[/*]
[*][b]Optional World Market:[/b] Computer IV and higher computers can open the existing board when [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/54255]Simple Trade World Market[/url] is installed. Simple Desktop works on its own; the market mod supplies its pricing features.[/*]
[/list][heading][color=#8FDAC0]🌱 Farm Computer information, by location[/color][/heading]
Learn the vanilla [b]Farm Computer crafting recipe[/b] to unlock [b]Farm Overview[/b] on any Computer I–VII. The app shows total crops, crops ready to harvest, unwatered crops, empty tilled soil, forage and ready machines. The main farm also shows hay storage and capacity, greenhouse crops ready, and whether the farm cave needs harvesting.

Use the location tabs for your [b]main farm, unlocked Greenhouse and Ginger Island farm[/b]. Visited modded maps can appear when they are marked as farms or greenhouses, including locations registered by Stardew Valley Expanded. This does not automatically include every map added by every mod.

Crop and forage counts belong to the selected map. Ready machines include its linked interiors, following vanilla Farm Computer scope. Each location stays separate; there is no combined total. Choose [b]Refresh[/b] for a new snapshot. The app is read-only and does not harvest or collect anything.

[heading][color=#C8B0F4]🎮 A game library for rainy afternoons[/color][/heading]
There are [b]sixteen custom games[/b] across the computer tiers:
[list]
[*]Chess and Reversi, with a casual computer opponent or shared-screen local two-player mode.[/*]
[*]Draw-one Klondike Solitaire and one-suit Spider Solitaire.[/*]
[*]2048 and Connect Four.[/*]
[*]Motor Dash, Unblock, Checkpoint Race and Cross Roads.[/*]
[*]A tile-swap Jigsaw Puzzle and the clue-based Find the Treasure.[/*]
[*]Minesweeper with safe opening squares, flags and three mine densities.[/*]
[*]Memory Match with native farm-item cards, three board sizes and relaxed or timed play.[/*]
[*]Snake with three speeds, pause and personal bests.[/*]
[*]Breakout with three lives, adjustable difficulty, mouse or directional paddle controls and personal bests.[/*]
[/list]Chess uses shaded, individually shaped pieces on a contrasting board. Solitaire and Spider use corner ranks, suit symbols and teal card backs; Spider shows full card faces at column ends. The other game screens use raised tiles, distinct tokens and restrained shading.

Rules are available inside each game. Snake and Breakout open paused, and their personal bests carry no rewards. Memory Match offers a timed option; new games, difficulty changes and mode changes ask for confirmation. Custom games have no gold or item stakes or prizes. Their progress is shared across your farm's capable computers and saves with the farm at the normal overnight save. Leaving without saving discards that day's game progress. Solitaire deals are not guaranteed to be winnable.

Computers VI and VII can also launch [b]Journey of the Prairie King and Junimo Kart practice[/b]. Junimo Kart still requires the Skull Key. Computer-launched practice preserves your existing Prairie King progress and blocks reward, achievement and high-score submissions. These practice sessions are not resumed through the custom game saves. Normal saloon arcade play is unaffected.

[heading][color=#9ACAF7]🎨 Eight desktop styles[/color][/heading]
Open [b]Settings[/b] in the top-right corner of the desktop or a custom game window, then [b]Themes[/b], to choose [b]Slate, Navy, Ocean, Forest, Lavender, Rose, Graphite or Aurora[/b]. Slate is the default. All eight styles pair a dark header and sidebar with light content panels.

Each style has a miniature desktop preview. [b]Saved[/b] marks your stored choice; [b]Preview[/b] marks an unsaved selection. Choose [b]Save[/b] to remember your style and UI size across all computer tiers. Cancel, Escape or controller B restores your previous choice. Arrow keys and controller directions follow the two-column theme grid.

[heading][color=#8FDAC0]📐 Choose your UI size[/color][/heading]
Open [b]Settings → UI size[/b] from the top-right corner of the desktop or a custom game window. Preview [b]75%, 90%, 100%, 110%, 125% or 150%[/b]; [b]100% is the default[/b]. Text, icons, artwork and click targets scale together.

Choose [b]Save[/b] to remember your UI size and theme. Cancel, Escape or controller B restores both previous choices. Large sizes fit automatically within the current screen without replacing your requested preference, so your chosen size returns when more space is available. At a standard 1920 × 1080 game UI viewport, 150% gives a 1500 × 930 computer window.

This setting applies to Simple Desktop menus and its sixteen custom games. Robin's normal shop, the native world map, text-entry overlays and native arcade practice retain their own game UI sizing.

[heading][color=#F2C879]⌨️ Controls and languages[/color][/heading]
Use the mouse to select apps, search and play. Keyboard navigation uses Tab/arrows, Enter/Space and Escape. Controller navigation uses directional inputs, A and B; game screens use X to switch between board navigation and buttons. Each game's Rules screen explains its controls.

Interface translations are included for [b]English, Chinese, French, German, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish[/b].

[heading][color=#8FDAC0]📦 Installation and compatibility[/color][/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Use [b]Stardew Valley 1.6.15 on PC[/b] with [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] [b]4.4.0 or later[/b].[/*]
[*]Extract the [b]SimpleComputerFurniture[/b] folder from the download into your game's [b]Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI, then visit Robin to buy your first kit.[/*]
[/list][b]PC single-player only.[/b] Android, multiplayer and split-screen are not supported. Simple Trade World Market is optional; the desktop launcher supports its version 1.12 board.

With [b]Simple Infinite Crafting and Cooking[/b] installed, computer recipes still require and consume their paid assembly kits and listed materials. Other crafting and cooking recipes follow that mod's settings.

[heading][color=#9ACAF7]💬 Bug Reports & Suggestions[/color][/heading]
Please include your game, SMAPI and mod versions, platform, expected and actual results, steps to reproduce, and a relevant [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log[/url]. A screenshot or short video can help. For suggestions, explain how the change would help your playthrough.
